We are given a rational $n\times r$ matrix $R$ and $d$ sparsity constants $s_i \le n$, and the goal is to find an $n\times d$ matrix $X$ with orthonormal columns that maximizes $\|R^\top X\|_F^2$, such that column $i$ has at most $s_i$ non-zero entries. Here $RR^\top$ plays the role of the covariance matrix and has rank at most $r$. We show that SPCA is NP-hard even when $r = d = 2$, but admits a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) when $r$ and $d$ are fixed. The returned solution has exactly orthonormal columns, and its entries are real algebraic numbers in an exact representation. For fixed $ε$, the number of steps of the algorithm is linear in $n$ up to a polylogarithmic factor. Our approach reduces SPCA to a sparse version of the orthogonal Procrustes problem, that is, to maximizing a linear function over the feasible region of SPCA. We show that this problem is NP-hard even for $d = 2$, and we give an FPTAS for it when $d$ is fixed. This FPTAS combines approximate dynamic programming over the rows, two-column updates that restore exact orthogonality, and an exact computation of the few variables for which these updates are not available.

Optimization and Control.title: The One-Skeleton of Multilinear Polytopes and Their Standard Relaxations
Optimization and Control.summary: Edge-following methods, such as the simplex method, move along edges of a polytope. Their behavior depends on which vertices are adjacent and on the diameter. We study both for the two polytopes of binary polynomial optimization: the multilinear polytope and its standard linear relaxation. For quadratic polynomials, Padberg showed that two integral vertices are adjacent in both polytopes if and only if the variables where they differ induce a connected subgraph. For higher degree, we replace this subgraph by a contracted hypergraph on the same variables, built from the monomials whose constraints tie these variables together. We show that its connectivity decides adjacency in the relaxation but, unlike in the quadratic case, not always in the multilinear polytope. Adjacency is the same in both polytopes exactly when the relaxation has the Trubin property. We investigate when this property holds and characterize it for cubic polynomials. The contracted hypergraph also yields short paths. The diameter of the multilinear polytope is at most the number of variables, and that of the relaxation is linear in the numbers of variables and monomials. Similar linear bounds hold for the number of pivots between bases of the relaxation.

Optimization and Control.title: Robust Safe Control Under Uncertainty: Estimation, Contraction, and Regret Bounds
Optimization and Control.summary: Disturbance uncertainty requires safety filters based on control barrier functions (CBFs) to leave a robustness margin, which can alter the nominal control input and degrade closed-loop performance. This paper studies safety and the resulting performance loss for discrete-time nonlinear systems with additive disturbances and polytopic input constraints. We develop a causal disturbance observer and construct two robust barrier conditions. The first uses a time-dependent bound on the estimation error. The second uses a constant margin when the disturbance increments are uniformly bounded and moves the requirement on the initial error from the online filter to an explicit initialization condition. For affine barriers, both filters are quadratic programs. We bound their input deviations from an oracle filter with access to the current disturbance and derive sufficient conditions for uniform contraction of the oracle closed loop. The contraction analysis accounts for state-dependent actuation, unmatched disturbances, and active physical input limits. Combining the sensitivity and contraction estimates gives finite-time dynamic regret bounds that quantify the effects of observer convergence, disturbance variation, and robustness margins. With sublinear cumulative certified disturbance variation and observer innovation error, the bounds yield sublinear regret.
Optimization and Control.comment: 15 pages, temporary, (optional) simulation to be added

Optimization and Control.title: Linearize or Discretize First? Error Estimates under Mesh-Uniform Regularity and Exponential Stability for the KdV Equation with Boundary Dissipation
Optimization and Control.summary:
We study the Korteweg-de Vries equation on a bounded interval with boundary dissipation, and its spatial semidiscretization by a weighted cubic Hermite Galerkin method. A small nonlinear wave can be approximated by a linear discrete simulation in two orders: linearize first and then discretize, or discretize first and then linearize. Both orders lead to the same total error. They divide this error differently between linearization and discretization. The difference of the two divisions is what we call the ordering error. We show that it is quadratic in the size of the initial datum and carries a positive power of the mesh size, for all time. It can be used to assess the effect of a coarse-mesh correction for nonlinear problems.
  For the continuous problem, the solution map is analytic, and the semigroup of the linearized equation has Crandall-Pazy regularity with the exact index 3/2. For the weighted scheme, the discrete semigroups of the linearized equation inherit exponential stability, Kato smoothing and Crandall-Pazy regularity, with bounds uniform in the mesh size. The nonlinear solution maps are analytic, also uniformly in the mesh size.
  These properties give error estimates in which the error and the datum are measured in the same norm: in the energy norm, in $H_0^1$ and in $H^2$. On every interval $[t_0,\infty)$, $t_0>0$, same-norm convergence holds uniformly on balls at algebraic rates. The ordering error is of order $h^{1/6}$ times the square of the energy norm of the datum, uniformly for all $t\ge0$.
Optimization and Control.comment: 36 pages. Ancillary files: the Lean 4 development for Theorems 4.1-4.4. Companion paper: arXiv:2611.12585

Optimization and Control.title: A Sequential Cubic Programming Method with Second-Order Complexity Guarantees for Equality Constrained Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop a new method for equality constrained optimization problems based on a sequential cubic programming framework. Each iteration utilizes a step decomposition based on the Jacobian of the constraints into a normal and a tangential component, the latter of which is found by solving a subproblem involving cubic regularization. The method incorporates second-order correction steps as necessary to ensure global convergence to second-order stationary points as well as local quadratic convergence. In addition, we show that the algorithm is the first to obtain worst case complexity guarantees on the order of $\mathcal{O}(ε_g^{-3/2})$ for the gradient of the Lagrangian, $\mathcal{O}(ε_H^{-3})$ in terms of second-order stationarity, and $\mathcal{O}(ε_c^{-1})$ in terms of the constraint violation. These are the best known complexity guarantees of any method for this class of problems.

Optimization and Control.title: Minimizing Monotone Norms in Fractional Load Balancing
Optimization and Control.summary:
We devise a fully polynomial time approximation scheme for minimizing a monotone norm $\left\lVert\cdot\right\rVert$ over a convex set $X\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$. We study the multi-customer setting, where $X=\sum_{i=1}^n X_i$ and the solution set $X_i\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}$ is given by a linear minimization oracle for each customer $i$. Our algorithm computes, for any given $\varepsilon>0$, a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate solution. With high probability, it uses $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}\left( \varepsilon^{-2}(n+d) \right)$ single-customer linear minimization oracle calls and the same number of generalized KL projections to the dual space $Y=\{y\in \mathbb{R}^d_{\geq 0}: \left\lVert y \right\rVert^* \le 1\}$. We assume no prior knowledge on $X$, and our running time depends only on $n$, $d$, and $\varepsilon$. Our result is robust in the sense that it allows for approximate linear minimization oracles and approximate KL projections. We show that the (approximate) KL projection can be performed efficiently for large classes of monotone norms, demonstrating the applicability of our approach.
  While such a result (with exact projection) is well-known for the $\ell_{\infty}$ norm via multiplicative weight updates and was recently obtained for ordered norms via a smooth norm approximation and a novel randomization, existing techniques do not extend to general monotone norms. In particular, a key feature used in previous proofs was dual price stability, which was derived from a global contraction property of the KL projection to the dual space $Y$. We show that this property does not extend to general monotone norms. Therefore, we use a different price mechanism, based on the well-known mirror descent paradigm, for which a local contraction property holds and guarantees stability.

Optimization and Control.title: Quadratic Convexification with Two Switching Variables via Extreme Rays
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider the convex hull of the quadratic lift $(x,xx^\top,y)$ of the set $\{(x,y) \mid 0 \le x \le y,\ y \in \{0,1\}^n \}$. Descriptions of this convex hull provide convex relaxations for quadratic optimization with switching variables, including problems with indefinite quadratic objectives and constraints. For $n=2$, we completely characterize the extreme rays of the corresponding cone of nonnegative quadratic functions, which consists of two switching rays, six boundary-product rays, discounted affine-square rays, and a parameterized family of discounted rank-two rays. These families generate the cone, so their linearizations give a complete valid-inequality description of the convex hull in the lifted space. The discounted rank-two rays also show that rank-one liftings cannot generate all valid inequalities. Using this classification, we prove a conjecture of Anstreicher and Burer on an exact semidefinite representation of this convex hull.

Optimization and Control.title: Trust-region high-index saddle dynamics for ill-conditioned saddle-point computation
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a trust-region high-index saddle dynamics (TRHiSD) framework for computing high-index saddle points in ill-conditioned problems. To address the deterioration of high-index saddle dynamics caused by inappropriate step sizes and search directions, we exploit its intrinsic local min--max structure and construct separate trust-region subproblems on the maximization and minimization subspaces to adapt the two trust-region radii to different local curvature scales. Under suitable assumptions and with exact spectral subspaces, we prove local linear convergence of the Cauchy-point variant and local quadratic convergence of the Newton-step variant. Numerical experiments on modified Rosenbrock functions are consistent with the predicted convergence rates. For the Landau--de Gennes model, a TRHiSD variant using a truncated conjugate-gradient step for the minimization subproblem substantially reduces the outer-iteration count and the wall-clock time in the tested cases.

Optimization and Control.title: Quantifying the Cost of Restoring AC Feasibility for Approximate Optimal Power Flow Solutions
Optimization and Control.summary: Power system operations rely on approximate solutions of the AC optimal power flow problem, most notably the DC optimal power flow used in security-constrained unit commitment and economic dispatch, while convex relaxations, machine learning surrogates, and other approximations are studied extensively in the academic literature. Because these approximations neglect or relax parts of the AC power flow equations, their solutions must be adjusted before dispatch; for example, the DC optimal power flow, which neglects transmission losses, reactive power, and voltage magnitude variations, is known to produce solutions that are always infeasible. The cost of this adjustment is not adequately understood. This paper proposes a method that quantifies, for any approximate solution, the minimum cost of the adjustments that restore AC feasibility, which is a lower bound on the cost of the heuristic adjustments used in practice. We apply it to the DC optimal power flow, the second-order cone and quadratic convex relaxations, and the AC optimal power flow solved to a loose relative tolerance of $10^{-4}$ instead of $10^{-8}$. Relative to the AC optimal power flow solution obtained from a local nonlinear optimization solver, and even with the minimum adjustment, the DC optimal power flow requires adjusting, on average, generators that account for 15.6% of total generation capacity and incurs a 1.10% cost increase; the convex relaxations require more adjustment (17.2% and 16.9%) but smaller cost increases (0.68% and 0.78%); and the loose-tolerance AC optimal power flow requires 6.1% and incurs 0.42%. These results indicate significant value in operating markets directly on the AC optimal power flow, which avoids the distortion of the dispatch and prices caused by heuristic feasibility restoration.
Optimization and Control.comment: 5 pages, 4 figures, submitted to 2027 IEEE Power & Energy Society General Meeting

Optimization and Control.title: Zeroes and Extrema of Functions via Random Measures
Optimization and Control.summary: We present methods that provide all zeroes and extrema of a function that do not require differentiation. Using point process theory, we are able to describe the locations of zeroes or maxima, their number, as well as their distribution over a given window of observation. The algorithms in order to accomplish the theoretical development are also provided, and they are exemplified using many illustrative examples, for real and complex functions.
Optimization and Control.comment: Corrected the dominating measure to have both atomic and nonatomic parts. Fixed typos. Function extrema and zeroes; Optimization; Poisson point process; Random counting measures; Riemann's zeta function

Optimization and Control.title: Contour-Assisted Evolutionary Computation: Estimating Peaks From the Contour Lines of Evaluated Solutions
Optimization and Control.summary: Evolutionary algorithms (EAs) evaluate many candidate solutions but use them mainly to rank individuals. This paper treats the evaluated solutions as the spot heights of a topographic survey and draws the contour lines they imply. The contour map decomposes the evaluated region into peaks: in two dimensions a contour tree with persistence separates significant peaks from interpolation ripples, and in more dimensions hill climbing on the interpolated surface locates the peaks and ray-cast level sets describe them. A memory of the explored peaks directs the search to new ones. The data-supported contours of each peak are extrapolated to zero size by an area law, exact for quadratic peaks and second-order accurate for smooth ones, that estimates a peak's location, height and shape before it is sampled. A contour-assisted EA (CA-EA) inserts contour steps with local search and peak memory into a genetic algorithm (GA), differential evolution or particle swarm optimization. A contour-assisted surrogate-assisted EA (CA-SAEA), for expensive problems, spends each evaluation on surrogate-screened offspring or on sampling around a peak, entered at the maximum of the interpolated surface. On 2-D benchmarks, CA-EA reduces the evaluations a plain GA needs by factors of 12 to 112; controls attribute its gain over classical memetic search to restarting local search on distinct peaks. On the CEC 2015 expensive suite in 10 and 30 dimensions, CA-SAEA has the second-best average rank, behind DYCORS and ahead of lq-CMA-ES and the competition winner MVMO, although in 30 dimensions MVMO wins significantly on 9 functions and loses on 6; there the map beats sampling around the best point on 5 of 15 functions and loses on 3. Entering the peaks at their extrapolated locations brought no gain at these budgets, although, with enough samples, it improves the estimated heights on most two-dimensional functions.
Optimization and Control.comment: 15 pages; supplementary material (10 pages) is provided as an ancillary file

Optimization and Control.title: Dynamic Programming for A Linear-Gaussian Dual Control Problem
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider an infinite-horizon discounted dynamic programming (DP) problem for a countable-innovation belief-state model. The model is a surrogate for a linear-Gaussian dual control problem involving an unknown parameter vector and Gaussian observation noise. The surrogate preserves the first two moments of the Gaussian innovation and the resulting posterior second-moment structure. We allow unbounded belief and control spaces and nonnegative stage costs with quadratic growth in the posterior mean and covariance. Using a posterior-moment weight, we show that the Bellman operator is a contraction in a weighted sup-norm space. We characterize the optimal cost as the unique solution of the Bellman equation in this space, establish the existence of optimal stationary policies. We further prove weighted sup-norm convergence of value iteration, policy iteration, and optimistic policy iteration under vanishing approximation errors. The convergence results under vanishing approximation errors rely on general weighted sup-norm contraction properties and are applicable beyond the particular dual control problem considered here.

Optimization and Control.title: Constructing option portfolio
Optimization and Control.summary: In this paper we consider the problem of constructing a portfolio composed of a set of financial options. We present a mixed-integer linear program. We apply our approach to index options for the S&P 500.

Optimization and Control.title: Controlling avalanche sizes in the Abelian sandpile model
Optimization and Control.summary: The Abelian sandpile model is a classical framework for studying large cascading events, such as those arising in models of forest fires and earthquakes. This work studies the control of such avalanches through the targeted removal of sand grains. We formulate this sequential control problem as an average-cost Markov decision process in which, before each grain addition, a controller may remove a sand grain from a selected vertex. The objective is to balance the long-run expected avalanche size against the cost of intervention. We analyze local intervention policies, which remove grains from a prescribed set of vertices whenever possible, and establish structural results for the recurrent classes and stationary distributions of the induced Markov chains. When the intervention set satisfies a property called topple-freeness, we sharpen these results, derive expressions for the gain and bias functions, and give necessary and sufficient conditions for optimality on general finite graphs. Finally, we apply the general theory to several specific graph classes and obtain a complete characterization of optimal policies on the one-dimensional lattice, the complete graph and the star graph for every value of the intervention cost.

Optimization and Control.title: A Generalization of the Passivity Theorem and the Small Gain Theorem Based on $ρ$-Stability, with Application to a Parameter Adaptation Algorithm for Recursive Identification
Optimization and Control.summary: The usual passivity theorem considers a closed-loop, the direct chain of which consists of a strictly passive stable operator $H_{1}$, and the feedback chain of which consists of a passive operator $H_{2}$. Then the closed-loop is stable. Let $ρ>1$. We show here that the closed-loop is still stable when the direct chain consists of a strictly $ρ^{-1}$-passive $% ρ^{-1}$-stable operator (a weaker condition than above) and the feedback chain consists of a $ρ$-passive operator (a stronger condition than above). Variations on the theme of the small gain theorem (incremental or not) can be made similarly. This approach explains the results obtained in a paper on identification which was recently published.

Optimization and Control.title: Duality for the Adversarial Total Variation
Optimization and Control.summary: Adversarial training of binary classifiers can be reformulated as regularized risk minimization involving a nonlocal total variation. Building on this perspective, we establish a characterization of the subdifferential of this total variation using duality techniques. To achieve this, we derive a dual representation of the nonlocal total variation and a related integration-by-parts formula, involving a nonlocal gradient and divergence. We provide such duality statements both in the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on proper metric spaces and for the space of essentially bounded functions on separable metric spaces. Furthermore, under some additional conditions we provide characterizations of the subdifferential in these settings.

Optimization and Control.title: Probabilistically Exact Convexification of Mixed-Integer Quadratic Optimization with Indicators
Optimization and Control.summary: We study the convexification of mixed-integer quadratic optimization with indicator variables. The problem remains NP-hard even when the quadratic matrix has bandwidth two, posing a fundamental obstacle to tractable exact convexification. To overcome this challenge in realistic settings, we introduce probabilistically exact (inner) convexification, a framework that relaxes the requirement of exactness for every objective while preserving exact optimality for statistically relevant ones. Our approach is motivated by inference applications, where the objective is determined by a data vector drawn from a distribution and a regularization vector chosen from a prescribed family. Our convexification preserves the exactness of the optimal value with high probability over the data distribution, simultaneously for every regularization vector in this family. We apply this notion to quadratic matrices of any fixed bandwidth. Despite their worst-case NP-hardness, we construct probabilistically exact convexifications that admit exact extended second-order cone formulations of size polynomial in the dimension $n$ and the inverse failure probability $1/δ$. The required assumptions for their high-probability exactness are surprisingly mild: they accommodate both light-tailed and heavy-tailed data, including distributions without finite mean, as well as arbitrary nonnegative regularization coefficients.

Optimization and Control.title: Precise Convergence Speed of Clipped SGD
Optimization and Control.summary: We present a tightened convergence analysis of clipped gradient descent on $(L_0, L_1)$-smooth functions, with quantitative constants. Building on the ideas of Koloskova et al (2023), we refactor several case disjunctions to reveal the central role of a control of the bias derived from fundamental properties of $\ell_2$-projection, simplifying proofs. We also extend the domain of validity from $η\leq 1 / (9 β)$ to $η< 1 /β$ where $β= L_0 + c L_1$ for clipping constant $c$, which matches the more traditional analysis of smooth functions. We strengthen the convergence criterion from $\left( \min_{t < T} \mathbb{E}[\lVert \nabla f(x_t) \rVert_2] \right)$ to $\left( \frac{1}{T} \sum_{t < T} \mathbb{E}[\lVert \nabla f(x_t) \rVert_2] \right)$ with matching speed, and lower the final achievable floor from $\mathcal{O}(\min(σ^2/c, σ))$ to the more precise $6 \min(σ^2 /c, 3 σ)$.
Optimization and Control.comment: v2 fixes several typos and clarifies some abuses of notations

Optimization and Control.title: Markov Population Potential Game: An Alternative Framework for Markovian Traffic Assignment
Optimization and Control.summary: Understanding the equilibrium behavior of large populations of interacting agents in transportation systems is challenging due to the high-dimensional state space and the coupled decision-making among agents. This study proposes the Markov population potential game (MPPG) that integrates Markov games, potential games, and population games as a unified framework for analyzing such interactions. The framework extends the classical Markov potential game to the population level and establishes theoretical conditions on stage rewards and state transitions under which the Markov population game admits a Beckmann-type potential function. Accordingly, every KKT point of the associated optimization problem yields an MPPG equilibrium. We further demonstrate that if only the reward condition holds, each KKT point of the optimization problem corresponds to a support-restricted $\varepsilon$-equilibrium, meaning the Q-values of any two active actions differ by at most $\varepsilon$, thereby significantly extending the applicability of MPPG. We further establish both priori and posteriori upper bounds of $\varepsilon$ to efficiently evaluate the approximation error. Inspired by the equivalent optimization problem, a projected-gradient (PG) policy iteration algorithm is developed. The theoretical bounds and PG algorithm are demonstrated through numerical experiments on a parametric Markov population game.

Optimization and Control.title: An efficient mixed-integer linear programming formulation for solving influence diagrams
Optimization and Control.summary:
Influence diagrams represent decision-making problems with interdependencies between random events, decisions, and consequences. Traditionally, they have been solved using tailored algorithms that determine the expected utility-maximizing decision strategy. Towards this end, most recent state-of-the-art solution approaches convert them into mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) models that can be solved using off-the-shelf MILP solvers. Computationally, these approaches are most efficient for influence diagrams that represent periodic (or sequential) decision processes, which can be cast as partially observable Markov Decision Processes. However, they are inefficient for problems that lack this periodic structure or whose influence diagrams have large state spaces.
  The efficient MILP formulation presented in this paper is specifically designed for influence diagrams that are challenging for earlier MILP formulations. Additionally, this formulation can be adapted to optimize conditional value-at-risk and to incorporate chance and logical constraints, thereby retaining the modeling flexibility of MILP-based methods. Finally, computational experiments on a range of problems from the literature are reported to show that the proposed formulation is much more efficient than earlier MILP formulations, particularly in problems which cannot be modeled as partially observable Markov decision processes and which lead to influence diagrams whose decision or chance nodes may have large state spaces.

Optimization and Control.title: Finite Element Approximation of Three-Dimensional Elliptic Optimal Control Problems with Curve-Supported Controls
Optimization and Control.summary: We consider a linear-quadratic elliptic optimal control problem in three dimensions with a box-constrained control supported on a compact embedded $C^{1,1}$ curve strictly contained in a bounded convex polyhedral domain. The right-hand side of the state equation is a measure supported on the curve, and the state is singular along it. We establish well-posedness and first-order optimality conditions and derive curve-adapted weighted inequalities and finite element error estimates for the singular state. For continuous piecewise linear finite elements on quasi-uniform tetrahedral meshes and variational discretization of the control, assuming exact integration over the curve, we prove the almost quadratic estimate $\|\bar q-\bar q_h\|_{L^2(γ)}\le Ch^2(1+\abs{\ln h})^3$. The proof of this estimate requires new results, which are of independent interest. The convergence rate observed in a numerical experiment is consistent with the predicted algebraic order.

Optimization and Control.title: Wolfe's Minimum-Norm-Point Method Generalizes the Simplex Method
Optimization and Control.summary: Wolfe's method computes the point of minimum Euclidean norm in the convex hull of finitely many points. The method is parameterized by an insertion rule and it has been an open problem whether Wolfe's original rule guarantees a polynomial number of iterations (De Loera, Haddock, and Rademacher; STOC'18). We resolve this question by proving an exponential lower bound. In fact, we establish a tight connection to the simplex method for linear programming that allows us to transfer many lower bounds for simplex pivot rules to corresponding insertion rules of Wolfe's method. These include not only Wolfe's linopt rule via Dantzig's pivot rule, but also many other classical, randomized and history-based rules. As a corollary, we obtain the first exponential example for the Lawson-Hanson algorithm for nonnegative least squares, as well as PSPACE-hardness of deciding whether the linopt rule ever uses a given point.
Optimization and Control.comment: v2: Lean formalization archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24136107; author emails; minor corrections

Optimization and Control.title: ReLU Networks for Model Predictive Control: Network Complexity and Performance Guarantees
Optimization and Control.summary: Recent years have witnessed a resurgence in using ReLU neural networks (NNs) to represent model predictive control (MPC) policies. However, determining the sufficient network complexity to ensure closed-loop guarantees remains a fundamental open problem. This involves a critical precision-complexity trade-off: undersized networks may fail to capture the MPC policy, while oversized ones may outweigh the benefits of ReLU network approximation. In this work, we project the MPC actions onto a tightened constraint set to satisfy the hard constraints, and establish a state-dependent Lipschitz continuity property for the optimal MPC cost function, which enables sharp convergence analysis of the closed-loop system. For the first time, we derive explicit bounds on ReLU network width and depth for approximating MPC policies with closed-loop guarantees. To reduce network complexity for the convergence to user-specified target sets, we propose a non-uniform error framework with a state-aware scaling function to adaptively adjust both the input and output of the ReLU network. Our contributions provide a foundational step toward certifiable ReLU NN-based MPC.

Optimization and Control.title: Matrix-Based Ant Colony Search with Batched Decoding for Hierarchical Replenishment Routing: A Stylized Case Study Based on Korean City Data
Optimization and Control.summary: We study a stylized single-vehicle replenishment-routing problem in which the cities of a national logistics network are both demand points and supply points: a vehicle of limited capacity delivers to every city once, and when its load is insufficient for the next city it must detour to a city already served that can still supply goods. A 100-node benchmark is built from Korean population and geographic data, with the cities divided into 10 levels; the per-visit supply coefficient and the allowed number of stops decrease geometrically with the level. Building on matrix-based ant colony optimization, we keep the states of the whole colony in arrays, couple route construction with a fixed greedy replenishment-decoding policy, and evaluate the candidate moves of a local search in batches. With frozen parameters and 30 runs on seeds never used for tuning, the matrix-based ant colony search with the batch local search (MACO) reaches a mean total distance of 3081.7 km; a genetic algorithm equipped with the same local search at the same frequency reaches 3074.9 km (no significant difference), and a MAX-MIN ant system with the same local search 3142.2 km. Ablation identifies the batch local search as the main contributor to solution quality; a load-aware transition factor gives no significant gain. Within the parameter ranges tested, raising the supply coefficients of the cities below the top level shortens the route more than relaxing the stop limits, which are not binding here.
Optimization and Control.comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables; code, data and raw records in the ancillary files

Optimization and Control.title: Hyperexponential Stabilization of Nonholonomic Systems by Oscillating Controls
Optimization and Control.summary: We address the problem of designing time-varying feedback controls that stabilize a given equilibrium of a nonholonomic system at a faster than the exponential rate. We consider systems with an arbitrary degree of nonholonomy and prove a theorem on practical hyperexponential stabilization under a suitable assumption on the parameterized dither signals. The convergence proof is based on a comparison equation with a prescribed power of logarithmic terms. We apply this result to stabilize a model of a car with two off-hooked trailers.
Optimization and Control.comment: Submitted to the European Control Conference (ECC 2027)

Optimization and Control.title: Learning Rate Transfer and Feature Learning Across Depth for Constrained Spectral Optimizers: Complete Scion
Optimization and Control.summary: Hyperparameter transfer across model depth is instrumental in training deep models, as it enables learning rates calibrated on shallow networks to be effectively applied to deeper architectures. The recent CompleteP framework establishes a $1/L$ residual scaling rule that demonstrates this for Adam-family optimizers. We study whether similar transfer extends to constrained optimization methods, specifically Frank-Wolfe and projected non-Euclidean normalized steepest descent, where updates are determined by linear minimization oracles. We derive scaling rules for these methods which confirm that the $1/L$ residual scaling applies, although the arguments differ from the Adam-family optimizers. Our analysis supports depth-wise transfer and width-wise transfer of the learning rate for the Scion algorithm while ensuring feature learning and avoiding the kernel-regime. In experiments on NLP transformers (nanoGPT on FineWeb), vision transformers (DeiT on ImageNet), and vision MLPs (MLP-Mixer on CIFAR-10), we observe learning rate transfer across depth and feature learning for appropriately chosen residual scaling.

Optimization and Control.title: Dual-Inertial Bregman Methods with Energy-Based Safeguarding
Optimization and Control.summary: We study dual-inertial (DI) Bregman proximal methods for convex optimization via an exact representation of the signed energy drift between dual-coordinate and primal affine interpolation. For unrestarted DI, bounded one-sided directional curvature gives a last-iterate objective-gap rate $\mathcal{O}((1+\log N)/N^2)$ after $N$ iterations, which improves to $\mathcal{O}(N^{-2})$ under weighted summability. The energy balance also provides a computable acceptance test, which we use in two safeguards. The restart safeguard attains a global $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$ rate after $T$ proximal calls, including rejected trials. Under local quadratic growth and kernel regularity, it restarts only finitely often and eventually converges linearly. The non-restarting safeguard preserves the quadratic weight recurrence via dual substeps. Every fallback terminates without triangle scaling, yielding a $\mathcal{O}(N^{-2})$ rate in outer iterations and an $\mathcal{O}(T^{-1})$ rate in calls, which improves to $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ when the cumulative fallback cost is $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Experiments on relative-entropy regression and nonnegative least squares illustrate the results.

Optimization and Control.title: Exact Decisions and Certified Values in $L_\infty$-Norm Computation from State-Space Representations
Optimization and Control.summary: Computing the $L_\infty$-norm of a time-invariant linear ordinary differential control system is a routine task in robust control, usually delegated to floating-point routines that perform well on most practical systems. Behind the numerical value, however, lies a discrete decision: whether a pole lies on the imaginary axis, and whether a mode of a realization is actually a pole of the transfer matrix. Floating-point arithmetic can only replace this decision with a tolerance. This paper explains, for a control audience, what reliable symbolic-numeric computation offers for this problem: exact arithmetic where a decision has to be made, and certified enclosures where a value has to be computed. We show how the problem is turned into a small polynomial system directly from state-space data, how this system is solved in practice, and what it costs. A benchmark on the {\tt COMPleib} library and on families of systems with known norms shows that two standard numerical routines err in opposite directions on the imaginary-axis decision, and never on the same system, while the certified method decides it correctly on every instance tested and computes the norm at a cost comparable to that of the numerical routines on most systems. We conclude with practical guidelines for users of numerical tools.
Optimization and Control.comment: 6 pages, 1 table. Submitted to the European Control Conference (ECC 2027)

Optimization and Control.title: Fast Subproblem Solving in Benders Decomposition for Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems with Topology Switching and Scenarios
Optimization and Control.summary: Potential-based flow problems arise for a range of practical problems, like the operation of lossless power networks. The distribution of flows through the network is governed by the potential equation, which relates arc flows and node potentials following arc potential functions. We consider a general variant with affine potential functions, topology switching, and scenarios. It can be solved using a Benders decomposition algorithm, with each scenario corresponding to a subproblem. Subproblem solving time can then significantly contribute to overall running time. We present a fast algorithm to obtain Benders optimality and feasibility cuts from fixed master solutions. Problems with affine potential functions are reduced to equivalent problems where every potential function is the identity function. Optimal primal and dual solutions as well as unbounded dual rays are determined by systems of linear equations (SLE), resulting in a constant number of SLEs solved per subproblem. SLEs are solved using LU-factorizations, with the similarity between primal and dual, scenarios, and master solutions exploited by reusing factorizations via low-rank updates to significantly reduce theoretical complexity. We demonstrate the method on security-constrained optimal transmission switching instances, where subproblem solve time reductions of 97.98 percent compared to a standard LP solver are observed.

Optimization and Control.title: On Star Monotone Operators: Theory and Applications
Optimization and Control.summary: Introduced by Solodov and Svaiter \cite{SS}, star monotone operators have repeatedly appeared as a sufficient condition ensuring global convergence of first-order algorithms, without requiring full monotonicity. Yet, despite this recurring role, a systematic study of the class itself has been missing from the literature. This paper fills that gap with the first comprehensive treatment of star monotone operators, a class that strictly encompasses monotone and pseudomonotone operators with nonempty zero sets, together with operators that are strongly quasimonotone along rays and satisfy a radial nondegeneracy condition. We develop basic calculus rules, existence and uniqueness results for zeros, global metric subregularity, and precise structural relationships with classical monotonicity notions. We further demonstrate the versatility of star monotonicity through a Clarke subdifferential characterization of nonsmooth star quasiconvexity, applications to Minty and Stampacchia variational inequalities, linear convergence guarantees for subgradient-type methods, and separable operators related to the Debreu--Koopmans problem.

Optimization and Control.title: Subgradient and Stochastic Finite-Difference Methods for Constrained Strongly Quasiconvex Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a projected subgradient method for solving quasiconvex minimization problems. By employing the Clarke subdifferential, we prove that the sequence generated by the proposed algorithm converges to a solution of the minimization problem when the objective function is locally Lipschitz continuous and strongly quasiconvex in the sense of Polyak, under the same assumptions required for convex functions with the convex subdifferential. Moreover, we derive explicit convergence rate estimates for both the iterates and objective function values. In particular, compared with the corresponding results for nonsmooth, locally Lipschitz, strongly convex optimization, our analysis replaces strong convexity with strong quasiconvexity while preserving the order of the convergence rate, thereby extending the guarantees to a class of possibly nonconvex objective functions. In addition, we investigate a stochastic finite-difference scheme for minimizing a strongly quasiconvex function subject to inequality constraints defined by strongly quasiconvex functions, and establish a convergence rate of order $O(k^{-1/4})$, consistent with known complexity bounds for stochastic zeroth-order methods.

Optimization and Control.title: A Monotone Meshfree-Particle Method for Mean Field Games on Scattered Point Clouds
Optimization and Control.summary: We develop a monotone meshfree--particle method for mean field games (MFGs). We discretize the backward Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation on a fixed scattered cloud, transport the forward Fokker--Planck law with reflected and killed particles, and close the fictitious-play loop by interpolation and mass-preserving kernel density estimation. Monotonicity is imposed row by row on two-dimensional clouds. Each row combines a positive generalized finite difference Laplacian with a nonnegative decomposition of the drift along rays to surrounding visible neighbors, with mirror images at reflecting walls, and every fixed-policy matrix is an M-matrix for arbitrary cell-Péclet number. We prove a discrete comparison principle and, on polygons with re-entrant corners included, that one HJB solve at a prescribed density converges to the viscosity solution off the boundary vertices, for convex Hamiltonians of at most quadratic growth under a structure condition. On a two-room floor plan with re-entrant door jambs, the computed HJB solutions converge to exact ones. A source-free exact MFG tests the fully coupled computation. At matched degrees of freedom on a grid domain, the meshfree HJB solve has a larger $L^2$ error and a smaller $L^\infty$ error than a five-point finite-difference solve, and is about twice as expensive including the stencil construction. On a non-convex evacuation game, the interior nodes of nine clouds receive monotone rows, apart from a few next to the boundary vertices that copy a neighbor.

Optimization and Control.title: $γ$-weakly $θ$-up-concavity: A Unified Framework for Non-Convex Optimization Beyond DR-Submodular and OSS Functions
Optimization and Control.summary: Many objectives in machine learning and combinatorial optimization are non-concave. We introduce $γ$-weak $θ$-up-concavity, a first-order condition for nonnegative monotone functions in which a scaling function $θ$ lets the curvature change with the size of the solution. The resulting class strictly contains monotone DR-submodular functions and One-Sided Smooth (OSS) functions. It also contains functions whose marginal gains first increase and then decrease, and functions that vanish faster than any power of the norm at the origin. We construct a surrogate gradient from gradients along the segment from the origin to the current point and prove an upper-linearization inequality with a point-dependent approximation coefficient. Restricting actions to the closed convex hull of the coordinate-wise maximal feasible points makes this coefficient uniformly positive, with a value determined by the curvature parameters and the geometry of the feasible set. Standard reductions to linear optimization then give offline approximation algorithms and online algorithms with regret guarantees. The coefficient matches the optimal one for DR-submodular maximization and improves the best known coefficients for OSS maximization over matroid constraints whenever the OSS parameter is positive.

Optimization and Control.title: Regularization and Full Support for the CBO Equation with Measure Initial Data
Optimization and Control.summary: We prove global well-posedness and regularization for the isotropic consensus-based optimization equation with initial probability measures of finite fourth moment. Under suitable weight decay assumptions, after any nonconstant consensus motion, both the density and the consensus trajectory become smooth, and all spatial Sobolev norms are locally bounded in time. The proof uses a Fourier commutator estimate, localization and iteration, followed by a nonlinear time bootstrap. Counterexamples show that smoothing can fail at a stationary consensus point. For non-Dirac initial data, we also prove positivity away from the consensus point and full support at every positive time in all dimensions.

Optimization and Control.title: Exact Output Steering with Vanishing Controls in Weighted Shift Dynamics
Optimization and Control.summary:
Exploiting the rich dynamics of wrapped weighted shifts and their residualizations, we characterize exact projected steering with vanishing initial controls.
  For wrapped shifts, steering is characterized by an expansive cycle multiplier and a residue separating the source and control channels. For residual shifts, a distinct spectral--toral mechanism emerges: steering through selected conjugate planes is equivalent to radial expansion and an arithmetic parity condition on phase resonances, yielding bounded-gap steering times and quantitative control estimates. For structured machine-learning representations built from orbit dictionaries, we derive a two-scale gain condition for steering coefficients while preserving decoded outputs.

Optimization and Control.title: Strategically Robust Linear Quadratic Dynamic Games
Optimization and Control.summary: We study linear quadratic dynamic games where players are uncertain about each other's control policies or goals and consequently seek to be strategically robust. Building on recent work on strategically robust and risk-averse game theory, we first formalize the problem of strategically robust linear quadratic dynamic games. We show that these can be rewritten as simple transformations of linear quadratic games in which each player chooses a controller in a fictitious game in which they are faced with an adversary who is penalized for deviating from the other players' policies. This formulation naturally induces a novel notion of dynamic equilibrium, which we call a strategically robust dynamic equilibrium. We establish existence and uniqueness (in the subgame-perfect sense) of such equilibria and show that the equilibrium policies are Markovian, linear, and can be efficiently computed via coupled backward Riccati equations. Through numerical simulations, including experiments in a network game, we illustrate the benefits of strategic robustness in designing robust and resilient decentralized control schemes. Our experiments also expose a "free-lunch" phenomenon in games in which robustness does not incur a corresponding loss in performance but can yield improvements in players' utilities and social welfare.
Optimization and Control.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables. Accepted to the 2026 IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC)

Optimization and Control.title: Relative-energy stabilization of an irreversible port-Hamiltonian tubular reactor
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper develops a relative-energy control approach for a boundary-controlled irreversible port-Hamiltonian model of a non-isothermal tubular reactor around a spatially nonuniform stationary profile. The starting point is a thermodynamic duality between the entropy-based availability used in earlier reactor control and the relative Hamiltonian induced by the irreversible port-Hamiltonian representation. Under physically interpretable stability conditions---positive heat capacity, positive compressibility and positive compositional susceptibility---the Hamiltonian density is shown to be strictly convex, while the corresponding entropy representation is strictly concave. The resulting relative Hamiltonian decomposes into kinetic, compressive, thermal and mixing contributions and yields an exact relative-energy balance in which irreversible dissipation is separated from profile-dependent terms. This structure leads to a bounded monotone distributed jacket feedback that injects thermal damping without cancelling the nonlinear PDE dynamics. A continuous coercivity condition gives a local a-priori decay estimate for sufficiently regular nonlinear solutions, while a composite energy functional provides an exponential estimate for the linearized closed-loop initial-boundary value problem. Structure-preserving PFEM simulations are used to verify the predicted dissipation mechanisms and constrained profile regulation.

Optimization and Control.title: Time-optimal problem in the space of probability measures
Optimization and Control.summary: This paper focuses on the value function in the time-optimal problem for a continuity equation in the space of probability measures. We derive the dynamic programming principle for this problem. Using this principle, we prove that the Kruzhkov transform of the value function is a unique discontinuous viscosity solution to the corresponding Dirichlet problem for the Hamilton-Jacobi equation. Finally, we establish the $Γ$-convergence of the value function in a perturbed problem to the value function in the unperturbed problem.

Optimization and Control.title: Frank-Wolfe Theorems for Mixed Integer Quadratic Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: The Frank-Wolfe theorem states that a quadratic function bounded from below on a polyhedron attains its infimum. We study when this remains true in the presence of integer variables, for sets defined by quadratic inequalities. Our main result is a complete classification for sets defined by convex quadratic inequalities with rational coefficients and a rational affine hull, a condition that holds for all full- dimensional sets. One integer variable never destroys attainment: if every rational quadratic objective that is bounded from below attains its infimum over the set, even after adding rational linear constraints, the same holds with one integer variable. In dimension at most 2, integer variables never destroy attainment. In dimension at least 3 and with two or more integer variables, attainment holds for every such objective if and only if the set has bounded curvature, that is, it is bounded except along directions in which all constraints are linear. Without convexity, these results remain valid, except that bounded curvature is no longer necessary. Moreover, integer variables can destroy attainment only if there are at least two of them and at least one continuous variable. The result for one integer variable follows from a lifting theorem, which also extends known results for cubic objectives and convex polynomial constraints. Finally, for convex constraints and rational data, attainment holds when the objective is bounded from above, convex, or quasi-convex over a full-dimensional convex set containing the feasible region.

Optimization and Control.title: RPX: Certifying Agent-Generated MILP Reformulations at Scale
Optimization and Control.summary: We present RPX, an independent certificate checker for AI-generated reformulations of mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs). RPX verifies that every feasible solution of either the original or the reformulated model can be converted into a feasible solution of the other with no worse objective value. This guarantees equal optimal values and enables solution recovery in the original variables. The checker derives the required checks directly from both models and verifies the certificate using exact arithmetic and reusable reconstruction rules. RPX certifies an agent-generated reformulation for each of the 240 instances in MIPLIB 2017 Benchmark v2. The source models contain up to 27.3 million matrix nonzeros. The median time to decode and check a certificate is 0.312 s, with a 95th percentile of 10.1 s.

Optimization and Control.title: Efficient Alternating Minimization with Applications to Weighted Low Rank Approximation
Optimization and Control.summary: Weighted low rank approximation is a fundamental problem in numerical linear algebra, and it has many applications in machine learning. Given a matrix $M \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$, a non-negative weight matrix $W \in \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}^{n \times n}$, a parameter $k$, the goal is to output two matrices $X,Y\in \mathbb{R}^{n \times k}$ such that $\| W \circ (M - X Y^\top) \|_F$ is minimized, where $\circ$ denotes the Hadamard product. It naturally generalizes the well-studied low rank matrix completion problem. Such a problem is known to be NP-hard and even hard to approximate assuming the Exponential Time Hypothesis [GG11, RSW16]. Meanwhile, alternating minimization is a good heuristic solution for weighted low rank approximation. In particular, [LLR16] shows that, under mild assumptions, alternating minimization does provide provable guarantees. In this work, we develop an efficient and robust framework for alternating minimization that allows the alternating updates to be computed approximately. For weighted low rank approximation, this improves the cost of each iteration of [LLR16] from $\|W\|_0k^2$ to $\|W\|_0 k$ where $\|W\|_0$ denotes the number of nonzero entries of the weight matrix. At the heart of our framework is a high-accuracy multiple response regression solver together with a robust analysis of alternating minimization. We also replace the random initialization of [LLR16], whose claimed guarantee fails, by subspace iteration from a Gaussian start, so our total running time of $\widetilde O((\|W\|_0 k+nk^3)\log(1/ε))$ includes the initialization. In exchange, our guarantee needs the weight matrix to be within spectral distance $γn$ of the all-ones matrix for a $γ$ that is polynomially small in $n$.
Optimization and Control.comment: ICLR 2025. This version replaces the random initialization, whose claimed guarantee fails, by subspace iteration, and states the main theorem with all the conditions it needs, including a stronger closeness condition on the weights. The running time bound is unchanged

Optimization and Control.title: Low Rank Matrix Completion via Robust Alternating Minimization in Nearly Linear Time
Optimization and Control.summary:
Given a matrix $M\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, the low rank matrix completion problem asks us to find a rank-$k$ approximation of $M$ as $UV^\top$ for $U\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times k}$ and $V\in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k}$ by only observing a few entries specified by a set of entries $Ω\subseteq [m]\times [n]$. In particular, we examine an approach that is widely used in practice -- the alternating minimization framework. Jain, Netrapalli, and Sanghavi [JNS13] showed that if $M$ has incoherent rows and columns, then alternating minimization provably recovers the matrix $M$ by observing a nearly linear in $n$ number of entries. While the sample complexity has been subsequently improved [GLZ17], alternating minimization steps are required to be computed exactly. This hinders the development of more efficient algorithms and fails to depict the practical implementation of alternating minimization, where the updates are usually performed approximately in favor of efficiency.
  In this paper, we take a major step towards a more efficient and error-robust alternating minimization framework. To this end, we develop an analytical framework for alternating minimization that can tolerate a moderate amount of errors caused by approximate updates. Moreover, our algorithm runs in time $\widetilde O(|Ω| k)$, which is nearly linear in the time to verify the solution while preserving the sample complexity. This improves upon all prior known alternating minimization approaches which require $\widetilde O(|Ω| k^2)$ time.
Optimization and Control.comment: ICLR 2024. This version corrects the algorithm and several proofs (sampling across rounds, initialization, the regression solver). The main theorem is unchanged

Optimization and Control.title: The optimization landscape of robust high-dimensional mean estimation: stability, moment adaptation, and mirror descent reweighting
Optimization and Control.summary: We study efficient robust estimation of a high-dimensional mean under strong contamination when the clean distribution has only $p\ge2$ moments, bounded by $ν_p$. We give a unified proof of stability for every $p\ge2$ with the optimal dimension-free sub-Gaussian rate, linking the reweighting, trimming and truncation techniques of the outlier and heavy-tailed robust literatures through concentration of counting and truncation processes. Building on stability and spectral signatures, we quantify the optimization landscape over sample weights that remove at most a fraction $\varepsilon_{n,k}=k/n$ of the mass, where the trimming parameter $k$ slightly exceeds the number of outliers. An unobserved convex spectral loss has inexact quadratic growth, with curvature $\frac{1-\varepsilon_{n,k}}{\varepsilon_{n,k}}$, relative to a mean-induced Bregman divergence, and the observable spectral loss supplies a dimension-free, inexact, relatively weakly star-convex subgradient oracle for it. This yields a Lyapunov analysis of mirror descent reweighting for $\varepsilon_{n,k}<\frac13$ that covers Hedge, the projected subgradient method, a new mean-induced mirror descent, and a centered multiplicative weights update. Each method uses one top-eigenvector computation per step and attains the optimal sub-Gaussian rate without knowledge of $(p,ν_p)$. Mean-induced mirror descent further achieves faster optimization rates and last-iterate guarantees, at the cost of a more expensive projection step in higher dimensions.

Optimization and Control.title: Local Linear Convergence of the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers for Semidefinite Programming under Strict Complementarity
Optimization and Control.summary: We investigate the local linear convergence properties of the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) when applied to Semidefinite Programming (SDP). A longstanding belief suggests that ADMM is only capable of solving SDPs to moderate accuracy, primarily due to its sublinear worst-case complexity and empirical observations of slow convergence. We challenge this notion by introducing a new sufficient condition for local linear convergence: as long as the converged primal-dual optimal solutions satisfy strict complementarity, ADMM attains local linear convergence, independent of nondegeneracy conditions. Our proof is based on a direct local linearization of the ADMM operator and a refined error bound for the projection onto the positive semidefinite cone, improving previous bounds and revealing the anisotropic nature of projection residuals. Extensive numerical experiments confirm the significance of our theoretical results, demonstrating that ADMM achieves local linear convergence and computes high-accuracy solutions in a variety of SDP instances, including those cases where nondegeneracy fails. Furthermore, we identify where ADMM struggles, linking these difficulties with near violations of strict complementarity-a phenomenon that parallels recent findings in linear programming.

Optimization and Control.title: Understanding the Asymptotic Transience of Q-Learning via Distributional Expansion
Optimization and Control.summary: Q-learning has been empirically observed to exhibit substantial transient error. This transient remains uncaptured by the leading Gaussian limit because the central-limit normalization removes the smaller-scale displacement generated by the initial nonlinear evolution. On the other hand, worst-case finite-sample guarantees, while accounting for transient effects, can obscure the mechanisms responsible for the error on a particular problem instance. We develop a finer asymptotic analysis that gives an asymptotically exact characterization of this transient for a fixed instance. Specifically, for synchronous Q-learning in finite discounted Markov decision processes, we separate the last-iterate error into an optimal-policy temporal-difference (TD) component and a nonnegative displacement caused by maximization. The centered TD component has Gaussian fluctuations at scale $n^{-1/2}$, whereas the maximization transient is of order $n^{-1}$ and converges almost surely, after rescaling by $n$, to a random limit. This limit represents the propagated effect of maximization errors generated before the greedy policy stabilizes. We combine this characterization with an Edgeworth expansion of the TD component to identify the corrections to its Gaussian approximation, separating the effects of initialization, non-Gaussian TD fluctuations, and maximization. The results reveal how transient errors arise for individual Q-learning instances and how their effects persist below the central-limit scale.

Optimization and Control.title: An Inexact Augmented Lagrangian Method for Semidefinite Complementarity Optimization
Optimization and Control.summary: Semidefinite complementarity constraints arise in applications such as inverse semidefinite programming and rank-constrained matrix optimization. We develop a structure-preserving augmented Lagrangian method (SPALM) for mathematical programs with these constraints. The method augments the smooth constraints and retains matrix complementarity in its subproblems. We handle these subproblems by an inexact proximal alternating framework with verifiable descent and stationarity conditions. With vanishing absolute subproblem errors, feasible accumulation points of infinite outer sequences are asymptotically M-stationary. Under AM-regularity, these points are M-stationary. We prove that active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ is sufficient for this regularity. For each AL subproblem, the full stationarity residual converges to zero along infinite accepted inner sequences if the initial sublevel set is bounded, the proximal parameters are bounded above and away from zero, and the block errors vanish. If the block errors are also square-summable, an $O(T^{-1/2})$ best-residual bound holds over $T$ accepted iterations. Huber-Stiefel and fixed-basis procedures generate feasible matrix candidates, whose acceptance is verified by descent tests and computable limiting-normal certificates. For rank-constrained correlation matrix approximation, we construct a lifting that preserves the projected feasible set and global optimal value and satisfies active-set SDCMPCC-LICQ at every feasible point. The stationarity guarantees apply to this lifted model. Finite-budget experiments on this lifting and a single-equality observation-fitting inverse SDP meet the prescribed numerical feasibility and stationarity tests in all 120 runs.

Optimization and Control.title: Random feature policy iteration for inverse mean field games with complex geometry and high dimensions
Optimization and Control.summary: We propose a random feature policy iteration method for reconstructing the obstacle function in a mean-field game (MFG) from observations of its value function, leveraging the method's mesh-free nature and flexibility to handle complex geometries and high-dimensional problems. The method builds on a policy iteration framework for inverse MFGs, which decouples the coupled nonlinear forward-backward PDE system into a sequence of linear PDE and inverse problem solves. The fixed random feature representations preserve this linear structure, allowing the resulting subproblems to be solved by minimizing residuals at sampled collocation points through linear least-squares problems. The mesh-free nature of the method further extends the applicability of the policy iteration framework to inverse MFGs with complex geometry and in high dimensions. Another key advantage is its flexibility in using different spatial approximations for different variables: the obstacle function, value function, and population density can be represented in separate feature spaces, accommodating obstacles that are substantially less regular than the corresponding PDE solutions. Moreover, boundary conditions can be enforced through collocation on irregular domains without constructing boundary-fitted meshes. Numerical experiments involving smooth and discontinuous obstacles, a domain with holes, and higher-dimensional problems demonstrate the accuracy and flexibility of the proposed method.

Optimization and Control.title: Nonlinear Eigen-approach ADMM for Sparse Optimization on Stiefel Manifold
Optimization and Control.summary: With growing interest in machine learning and data science, creating efficient algorithms to optimize various dimension reduction objectives has become particularly important. This paper is concerned with optimization problems on the Stiefel manifold whose objective functions take the form as the sum of a smooth function and a nonsmooth one. A common practice is to split such a problem into a smooth optimization subproblem on the Stiefel manifold and a nonsmooth one and solve them by some version of the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Usually the smooth subproblem is solved by standard optimization techniques skillfully adapting to the manifold. However, often the smooth subproblem has strong linear algebra characteristics which, if carefully exploited, can lead to much more efficient solvers than the standard optimization techniques that ignore the characteristics. In this paper, it is proposed to tackle the smooth subproblem through a nonlinear eigen-approach which can fully utilize rich linear algebra structures that dominantly present in objective functions from today's data science applications. We conduct convergence analysis and analyze computational complexity for obtaining an $ε$-stationary point. Numerical experiments demonstrate the advantages of the proposed algorithm compared to the state-of-the-art approaches.

Optimization and Control.title: Splitting and Alternating Minimization Methods for Training Orthogonal Deep Feedforward Networks
Optimization and Control.summary: Training deep feedforward networks with weight matrices constrained to layer-wise Stiefel manifolds serves as an effective regularization technique to improve generalization. However, the simultaneous presence of orthogonality constraints and nonsmooth activation functions poses severe theoretical and computational challenges for standard stochastic gradient and Riemannian optimization methods. In this paper, we propose two splitting and alternating-based algorithms to train orthogonal deep feedforward networks (OrthDFNs). By introducing auxiliary variables, we decouple the nested nonsmooth compositions and manifold constraints into a structured equality-constrained optimization problem. To solve this model, we develop OrthALM, an inexact augmented Lagrangian method (ALM) that employs a proximal alternating minimization scheme to solve its subproblems. Crucially, every block coordinate subproblem admits an exact, closed-form solution. We establish a rigorous convergence theory for OrthALM, proving that every accumulation point of the generated sequence is a Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) point of the regularized, reformulated problem. Furthermore, we introduce OrthADMM as a practical, proximal-free variant that executes a single inner alternating sweep per multiplier update to accelerate computation. Extensive numerical experiments show that OrthALM attains lower training error and constraint residuals than OrthADMM in most configurations. OrthADMM achieves competitive test accuracy and the lowest reported runtime in most comparisons with the selected baselines.
